Customer Acquisition.title: Fix Google Ads conversion inefficiency
Customer Acquisition.whats_happening: Google Ads has the lowest conversion rate at 11.18% with a CPA of $3.90, indicating poor traffic quality despite reasonable CTR of 4.72%.
evidence: Google Ads CVR (11.18%) is the lowest across all 6 channels
CTR at 4.72% is mid-range so visibility is not the problem — conversion is
CPA at $3.90 is 4.7x higher than SMS ($0.83)

what_you_should_do.step: Audit search terms report and exclude low-intent queries
what_you_should_do.how: Review last 30 days of search terms, identify queries with clicks but zero conversions, add as negative keywords
guardrails: Do not exclude branded terms
Preserve queries with fewer than 10 clicks — insufficient data

what_you_should_do.step: Test dedicated landing pages for Google Ads traffic
what_you_should_do.how: Create landing page with messaging matched to high-intent search queries and A/B test against current generic page
guardrails: Run test for minimum 2 weeks
Ensure conversion tracking is verified before launch

Customer Acquisition.why_this_matters: Google Ads consumes $320 (19.6% of total budget). Improving CVR from 11.18% to 13% would generate approximately 15 additional conversions at the same spend.

expected_impact.explanation: Better keyword targeting and landing page relevance should improve CVR from 11.18% toward 13%.

dependency_or_risk: Requires access to Google Ads search terms report
Landing page changes need design and development resources

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Compare Google Ads conversion rate and CPA week-over-week after changes
measurement_plan.success_criteria: Conversion rate improves to 13% or above within 3 weeks
measurement_plan.notes: If CVR does not improve, consider reducing Google Ads budget and reallocating

Customer Acquisition.title: Scale SMS — cheapest and highest converting acquisition channel
Customer Acquisition.whats_happening: SMS has the lowest CPA at $0.83 and the highest conversion rate at 19.64%, but receives only $40 spend (2.5% of total budget).
evidence: SMS CPA ($0.83) is 5.3x cheaper than Facebook ($4.40)
SMS CVR (19.64%) is the highest across all channels
SMS spend ($40) is only 2.5% of total budget — severely underinvested

what_you_should_do.step: Increase SMS campaign frequency and audience size
what_you_should_do.how: Expand subscriber lists through website opt-in and checkout capture, increase send frequency by 20-30%
guardrails: Monitor opt-out rates weekly — pause if unsubscribes exceed 2%
Do not send more than 3 SMS per week

Customer Acquisition.why_this_matters: Shifting $100 from Facebook to SMS would theoretically acquire 120 additional customers at SMS efficiency versus 23 at Facebook rates.

expected_impact.explanation: Higher SMS spend at current efficiency should acquire significantly more customers per dollar.

dependency_or_risk: SMS efficiency may degrade at higher volumes
Requires sufficient subscriber base to scale

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Track SMS CPA and new customers weekly as spend increases
measurement_plan.success_criteria: SMS CPA stays below $1.50 at increased volume
measurement_plan.notes: If CPA rises above $1.50, stabilise at last efficient spend level

Customer Acquisition.title: Scale Email — second most efficient acquisition channel
Customer Acquisition.whats_happening: Email has a CPA of $1.47 and conversion rate of 13.33% on only $100 spend, making it the second most efficient acquisition channel after SMS.
evidence: Email CPA ($1.47) is 2.7x cheaper than Google Ads ($3.90)
Email CVR (13.33%) is the second highest after SMS
Email spend ($100) is only 6.1% of total budget

what_you_should_do.step: Increase email campaign volume and list growth
what_you_should_do.how: Add email capture at every customer touchpoint, launch a welcome series for new subscribers, increase campaign sends by 25%
guardrails: Maintain list hygiene — remove hard bounces immediately
Segment sends to avoid fatigue on engaged subscribers

Customer Acquisition.why_this_matters: Email is already the second cheapest channel for customer acquisition. Growing the list and send volume extends this advantage.

expected_impact.explanation: Higher email volume at current efficiency should grow new customer count without proportional CPA increase.

dependency_or_risk: List growth takes time — not an overnight fix
Over-sending risks higher unsubscribe rate

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Track Email CPA, list size, and new customers weekly
measurement_plan.success_criteria: Email CPA stays below $2.50 while new customers increase by 20%
measurement_plan.notes: Monitor unsubscribe rate as a leading indicator of fatigue

Customer Acquisition.title: Investigate Facebook's weak acquisition performance
Customer Acquisition.whats_happening: Facebook has the highest CPA at $4.40, lowest CTR at 4.0%, and lowest ROAS at 5.0 — the weakest paid channel across all acquisition metrics.
evidence: Facebook CPA ($4.40) is the highest across all channels
Facebook CTR (4.0%) is the lowest across all channels
Facebook ROAS (5.0) is the lowest across all channels
Instagram uses the same ad platform but outperforms on CTR (4.4%) and ROAS (7.11)

what_you_should_do.step: Audit Facebook audience targeting and creative
what_you_should_do.how: Check audience overlap with Instagram, review creative by format, test Advantage+ audiences
guardrails: Maintain minimum spend for retargeting
Run audience tests for at least 7 days before evaluating

Customer Acquisition.why_this_matters: Facebook consumes $220 (13.5% of total budget) with the worst efficiency metrics. Improving or reallocating this spend has material impact.

expected_impact.explanation: Better targeting should reduce CPA from $4.40 closer to Instagram's $4.09 as a first milestone.

dependency_or_risk: Changes to Facebook targeting may affect Instagram delivery via shared Meta platform
If Facebook cannot improve, budget should be reallocated

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Compare Facebook CPA and CTR weekly after targeting changes
measurement_plan.success_criteria: CPA drops below $4.00 and CTR improves above 4.5% within 4 weeks
measurement_plan.notes: If no improvement after 4 weeks, reduce Facebook to retargeting-only

Customer Acquisition.title: Reduce Email bounce rate to protect conversion efficiency
Customer Acquisition.whats_happening: Email has the highest bounce rate at 0.36 despite the second-best conversion rate at 13.33%. Potential customers are lost before converting.
evidence: Email bounce rate (0.36) is the highest across all channels
Email CVR (13.33%) is strong — those who stay convert well
SMS bounce rate (0.19) shows what well-aligned messaging achieves

what_you_should_do.step: Optimise email landing pages for relevance and speed
what_you_should_do.where: Website landing pages for Email campaigns
what_you_should_do.how: Match landing page headline to email subject line, test page load time, simplify to fewer than 3 conversion steps
guardrails: Use UTM parameters to isolate Email traffic
Do not change other channel landing pages during test

Customer Acquisition.why_this_matters: Reducing bounce rate from 0.36 to 0.25 could recover 10-15% more conversions from existing email volume at no additional spend.

expected_impact.explanation: Better message-to-landing-page alignment should reduce bounce rate from 0.36 toward 0.27.

dependency_or_risk: Requires web development resources
Some bounce may be driven by list quality not landing page

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Track Email-specific bounce rate and CVR weekly
measurement_plan.success_criteria: Bounce rate drops below 0.28 within 3 weeks
measurement_plan.notes: If no improvement, investigate email list quality and segmentation

Customer Acquisition.owner_suggestion: Email marketing and web development teams

Customer Satisfaction.title: Reduce Email bounce rate — highest across all channels

evidence: Email bounce rate (0.36) is the highest across all channels

Test one variable at a time — email content or landing page, not both

Customer Satisfaction.why_this_matters: Email is the second most efficient acquisition channel. Reducing bounce unlocks more conversions from existing volume at no cost.

expected_impact.explanation: Better alignment should reduce bounce from 0.36 toward the channel average of 0.27.

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Track Email-specific bounce rate weekly

Customer Satisfaction.title: Monitor Instagram frequency to prevent ad fatigue

evidence: Instagram frequency (2.8) is elevated
TikTok frequency (3.5) is higher but engagement remains strong — TikTok audiences tolerate higher frequency
Instagram engagement (5.6%) is healthy but could decline with fatigue

guardrails: Do not set cap below 2.0 — insufficient exposure
Track engagement by creative variant to identify fatigue early

Customer Satisfaction.why_this_matters: Ad fatigue is a leading cause of declining engagement and rising CPM. Proactive management prevents this.

expected_impact.explanation: Frequency caps and rotation should maintain the 5.6% engagement rate and prevent decline.

dependency_or_risk: Caps may reduce reach if audience is small
Rotation requires ongoing content production

measurement_plan.notes: If engagement drops below 5% despite rotation, investigate audience saturation

Customer Satisfaction.title: Reduce Facebook bounce rate to improve user experience
Customer Satisfaction.whats_happening: Facebook bounce rate is 0.34, the second highest after Email (0.36), suggesting ads are setting expectations the landing page does not meet.
evidence: Facebook bounce rate (0.34) is the second highest
Facebook engagement rate (5.36%) is already the lowest among social channels
High bounce compounds the engagement problem — users leave quickly

what_you_should_do.step: Test landing page variants for Facebook traffic

guardrails: Isolate Facebook traffic using UTM parameters
Run A/B test for minimum 2 weeks

expected_impact.explanation: Landing page alignment should reduce Facebook bounce from 0.34 toward 0.25.

dependency_or_risk: Requires web development resources
If ad creative is the problem, landing page fixes alone won't help

measurement_plan.how_to_measure: Track Facebook-specific bounce rate and time-on-page
